# Psalm 86 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A prayer of David. Listen to me, LORD, and answer — I'm poor and I need you.

**2** Protect my life because I'm devoted to you. Save your servant — I trust you, my God.

**3** Be kind to me, Lord — I'm calling out to you all day long.

**4** Bring joy to your servant's heart, because I'm lifting my whole self up to you, Lord.

**5** You, Lord, are good and ready to forgive, overflowing with love for everyone who calls on you.

**6** LORD, please hear my prayer! Pay attention to my cries for help.

**7** When I'm in trouble, I call out to you because you always answer me.

**8** There is no god like you, Lord! Nothing compares to what you do.

**9** Every nation you've created will come and kneel before you, Lord, and bring honor to your name.

**10** Because you are great — you do miraculous things! You alone are God.

**11** Teach me how to live your way, LORD, and I'll walk in your truth. Give me an undivided heart that honors your name.

**12** I will praise you, Lord my God, with everything I have, and I will bring glory to your name forever.

**13** Your faithful love for me is enormous — you pulled me back from the brink of death.

**14** God, arrogant people have come after me; a gang of violent men is trying to kill me — they couldn't care less about you.

**15** But you, Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God — slow to get angry, rich in love and faithfulness.

**16** Turn toward me and show me grace. Give your strength to your servant; save the child of your servant.

**17** Give me some unmistakable sign of your goodness, so those who hate me will see it and be put to shame — because you, LORD, have helped and comforted me.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **86:11**: 'Give me an undivided heart' — this might be the most honest prayer in the Bible. We don't just need guidance; we need the inner unity to actually follow it. Half our problem is that our heart wants two things at once.

- **86:15**: This verse is essentially God's résumé — his self-description from Exodus 34:6. Whenever someone in the Bible needs to remind God who he is, they quote this. It's the most-referenced verse about God's character in the entire Old Testament.

— PNEUMA
